sources.title: NPR Topics: Home Page Top Stories

articles.author: Chandelis Duster
articles.description: The route for the iconic cycling race's final stage was shortened because security and police were reassigned to assist with wildfires in southwest France.
articles.title: Tadej Pogačar of Slovenia wins the 2026 Tour de France, his fifth victory in the race

articles.author: The Associated Press
articles.description: The United States paused attacks on Iran for a second straight day Sunday and Tehran said it had done so too, as efforts continued to bring the countries back to negotiations on an interim ceasefire.
articles.title: U.S. pauses attacks on Iran for a second straight day and Tehran does too

articles.author: David Folkenflik
articles.description: A year after President Trump signed a law ending six decades of federal funding of public media, it's a time of reinvention, innovation and clear anxiety at public tv and radio stations nationwide.
articles.title: Rage-giving, innovation and cuts: How public media has survived without federal funds

articles.author: Jane Arraf
articles.description: Unable to return home, some Lebanese displaced by Israel's invasion of southern Lebanon are buying satellite images to see whether their houses survived.
articles.title: Lebanese displaced by war turn to satellites to check their homes

articles.author: Maria Godoy
articles.description: For decades, ADHD was viewed as a childhood condition that mostly affected boys. Researchers now know ADHD manifests differently in girls, but many still go undiagnosed until adulthood.
articles.title: ADHD looks different in women and poses unique health risks

articles.author: Kadin Mills
articles.description: Many Native American languages are endangered. With the help of his mentor, a 12-year-old in Michigan hopes to help preserve his language through robotics.
articles.title: Meet the robots programmed by kids to speak their Indigenous languages

articles.author: Ava Berger
articles.description: When summer rolls around, many parents scramble to sign up their young kids for outdoor activities. But what do you do when extreme heat and wildfire smoke increasingly make the outdoors dangerous?
articles.title: Climate change is now threatening a pillar of childhood: summer break

articles.author: Chandelis Duster
articles.description: Germany's interior minister Alexander Dobrindt described the incident as a likely "Islamic terror attack," and named the suspect as Abdul Ballout, who was born in Germany and has Lebanese roots.
articles.title: Suspect in Berlin Pride vehicle attack is dead, police say

articles.author: Chandelis Duster
articles.description: In France, around 50,000 people were evacuated from their homes overnight into Sunday, according to interior minister Laurent Nuñez. At least one person has died in a fire in Spain, officials said.
articles.title: France and Spain fires force more than 300,000 to flee homes

articles.author: Nina Totenberg
articles.description: Former President Joe Biden is declining to appeal a court ruling that allows the Justice Department to publicize recordings of conversations between him and a writer collaborating on his memoir.
articles.title: Biden ghostwriter tapes to be released

articles.author: Achol Arok (now), Stephanie Convery (earlier)
articles.description:
Follow the day’s news live

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

What you need to know about today’s AusAlert test

It’s also well worth watching this video of Guardian Australia’s community affairs reporter Adeshola Ore’s interview with Barnaby Joyce about Armidale’s refugee resettlement program and One Nation’s policy positions on immigration.
One Nation’s policy is that immigrants who do not speak English should “under no circumstances … be able to settle in Australia”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Australia news live: seven new suspected bird flu cases in SA as conservation charity warns ‘this is evidence of spread’

articles.author: Petra Stock
articles.description:
More electric vehicles sold in first half of 2026 than whole of last year, new data shows

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Australians bought more electric vehicles in the first six months of 2026 than the whole of the previous year, new data shows, as the ongoing crisis in the Middle East causes uncertainty about petrol prices.
There were 103,855 battery electric vehicles (EVs) sold nationally between January and June, compared with 103,269 in 2025, according to data from VFacts and the Electric Vehicle Council.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘A new trajectory’: EVs now almost quarter of Australia’s new car sales as fuel crisis bites

articles.author: Associated Press in Seattle
articles.description:
At least four people taken to hospital with one reported to be in a critical condition after gunfire at Seattle Center near Space Needle
At least four people including a child were wounded in a shooting on Sunday night at an events complex close to the Space Needle in Seattle, a hospital spokesperson said.
The Seattle Center was hosting the Bite of Seattle food festival over the weekend. After the shooting, police urged people to avoid the area.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Shootings at Bite of Seattle food festival leave several injured

articles.author: Benita Kolovos Victorian state correspondent
articles.description:
Deputy premier says he told leader of his intention on Monday after Allan refused request to stand down

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Victoria’s deputy premier, Ben Carroll, has confirmed he will nominate for the leadership of the Labor party, after a group of MPs told Jacinta Allan she no longer had the support of caucus.
The cross-factional group of ministers and MPs met the premier before Monday’s scheduled cabinet meeting, to tell her she had lost the majority of support and urged her to stand down, just four months before the state election.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Jacinta Allan leadership challenge: Ben Carroll confirms he will stand against Victorian premier

articles.author: Josh Butler
articles.description:
National emergency test alert will be sent to all compatible mobile devices on 27 July, with domestic violence advocates advising how to turn off safe phones

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Virtually every phone in the country will blare an emergency siren at 2pm AEST on Monday 27 July as part of the first Australia-wide test of a new national warning system called AusAlert.
Most phones, and some smartwatches and tablets, will receive a pop-up notification and an alert sound that cannot be silenced – even if your device is on “do not disturb” or silent mode.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: AusAlert test: what time will national emergency warning siren sound on phones in Australia today? Here’s what to know

articles.author: Associated Press
articles.description:
Southern and central states from California to Mississippi face heat indexes above 100F amid another heat dome
At least 40 million people were under extreme heat warnings across central and southern parts of the United States on Sunday as high temperatures and severe humidity gripped large swaths of the country for a second straight day.
Heat indexes well above 100F (38C) stretched from Minnesota down to Mississippi, extending west into southern California and Nevada. Parts of the south-west were expected to see highs of 120F (49C), according to the National Weather Service.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Extraordinarily hot’: US heatwave stretches on with millions still under warnings

articles.author: Josh Halliday North of England editor
articles.description:
PM urged to end ‘cover-up culture’ and order independent review taking in evidence that has emerged on 1994 crash
The families of those killed in an RAF Chinook crash in 1994 have urged Andy Burnham to end Britain’s “cover-up culture” and order an independent review into the disaster.
Twenty-nine serving military personnel died when the Chinook HC2 helicopter crashed on the Mull of Kintyre in south-west Scotland during a flight from Northern Ireland.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: RAF Chinook crash victims’ families ask Andy Burnham for review of disaster

articles.author: Phillip Inman
articles.description:
Bank of England expected to keep rates on hold on Thursday but renewed Iran conflict casts shadow over energy costs
The Bank of England could be forced to tear up its economic forecasts and raise interest rates later this year if oil prices return to above $100 a barrel, according to City economists.
Before a meeting of Bank officials on Thursday, economists said that while an interest rate hike would probably be avoided this week there could be some in the future because of conflict in the Middle East.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Rising oil prices could force up UK interest rates, say economists

articles.author: Marina Dunbar
articles.description:
Figures are source of dispute as US defense department days ago reduced record of troops killed and wounded
The Pentagon updated its official war casualty database over the weekend, adding more than 140 wounded service members. The Defense Casualty Analysis System (DCAS) also introduced a new casualty category labeled “Overseas Operations” for personnel killed and wounded “starting July 7”.
According to the updated database, the official toll for the earlier phase of the US-Iran war, known as Operation Epic Fury, now stands at 14 service members killed and more than 400 wounded in action.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Pentagon reports more than 600 Iran war casualties in quiet database update

articles.author: Nadeem Badshah
articles.description:
Four others arrested on suspicion of same murder in Luton after death of 17-year-old
A 16-year-old boy has been charged with murdering a teenager who died from multiple stab wounds at a park in Luton, police said.
Four other teenagers have been arrested on suspicion of the same murder.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Boy, 16, charged with murder of teenager stabbed in Luton park

articles.author: Jamie Grierson
articles.description:
Airport’s bars and restaurants were also unable to serve drinks to passengers because of lack of running water
Water supply has been restored to most of Gatwick airport after passengers spent hours without access to working toilets, and bars and restaurants were closed.
Most toilets had reopened across both terminals on Sunday evening, with the remaining facilities, including bars and restaurants, expected to return to normal for the first of Monday’s flights.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Water supply restored to Gatwick airport after hours without working toilets

articles.author: Peter Walker Senior political correspondent
articles.description:
Ukrainian president will be first overseas visitor for new British prime minister
Volodymyr Zelenskyy will become Andy Burnham’s first overseas visitor as prime minister, in a visit that Burnham said underlined Britain’s “unwavering” backing for Ukraine.
Less than two weeks after Keir Starmer travelled to Kyiv for the final foreign visit of his prime ministership, the Ukrainian president will on Monday join Burnham at a naval base where Ukrainian forces have been receiving training.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Burnham to meet Zelenskyy at UK naval base in show of ‘unwavering’ support

articles.author: Associated Press
articles.description:
Israeli prime minister says ICC’s war crime charges are ‘bogus’ and plans to be in New York for UN gathering this fall
Benjamin Netanyahu said on Sunday that Zohran Mamdani, the New York City mayor, is “fomenting hate” by calling the Israeli prime minister a war criminal who should be arrested over Israel’s war in Gaza if he visits the city for the United Nations general assembly.
Netanyahu said he intends to be in New York in September to address the annual UN gathering of world leaders, despite the mayor’s suggestion that he is not welcome. Mamdani said on Wednesday that while New York City does not have legal authority to execute an arrest warrant issued by the world’s top war crimes court, he encouraged the federal government to do so.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Netanyahu accuses Mamdani of ‘fomenting hate’ in calls for PM’s arrest

articles.author: Marina Dunbar
articles.description:
Scott Gottlieb responds to report that company contacted the White House seeking to delay a recall announcement
Former Food and Drug Administration commissioner Dr Scott Gottlieb said on Sunday that it was “not standard operating procedure” for Taylor Farms to ask the White House to intervene as the company prepared to announce a recall tied to a massive cyclospora outbreak.
Appearing on CBS’s Face the Nation, Gottlieb was asked about a report from the Wall Street Journal that Taylor Farms contacted the White House seeking to delay a recall announcement while federal investigators were preparing to publicly link the company to the multi-state outbreak.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Not standard’ for Taylor Farms to ask White House to delay cyclospora recall, ex-FDA head says

articles.author: Andrew Roth in Jerusalem
articles.description:
Top military officials say campaign has reached its limit of effectiveness and warn of dwindling stocks of munitions
The US has paused strikes on Iran for a second night as top military officials advised Donald Trump to halt his bombing campaign, and diplomatic negotiations have continued to avoid a return to all-out war.
Trump is said to be weighing up diplomatic and military options in the nearly five-month-old conflict, with Benjamin Netanyahu expected to visit the White House on Tuesday. The Israeli prime minister is a vocal critic of Washington’s negotiations with Iranian leaders and has pressed for the US to continue its strikes against Iran.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: US pauses Iran attacks for second night after Trump advised to halt bombing

articles.author: Maya Yang
articles.description:
Tom Homan comments on officer’s eligibility to serve after reports that agent’s two ex-wives had accused him of abuse
Tom Homan, the Trump administration “border czar”, on Sunday said he did not believe the Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officer at the center of a recent fatal shooting in Maine “should have ever cleared vetting”.
Speaking to CNN’s State of the Union, Homan was asked by host Dana Bash about the officer’s eligibility to serve following reports that two of his ex-wives had accused him of abuse.
The Associated Press contributed reporting
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump ‘border czar’ says ICE officer in Maine killing should not have cleared vetting

articles.author: Deborah Cole in Berlin and Jennifer Rankin
articles.description:
Abdul Ballout, 21, reportedly shot in operation at allotment in Spandau district after fatal attack in Tiergarten park
A man suspected of driving a van into a crowd near Berlin’s Pride festival then going on a knife rampage in an Islamist terror attack has been shot dead by police, German officials have said.
Police confirmed on Sunday evening that the chief suspect had been shot dead, reportedly during an operation at an allotment garden complex ⁠in the capital’s Spandau district.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Police shoot dead Berlin Pride van and knife rampage suspect, officials say

articles.author: Nadeem Badshah and agencies
articles.description:
Director Ryan Coogler announces British actor in lead role alongside co-stars Letitia Wright and Winston Duke

The British actor David Jonsson has been unveiled as the new Black Panther by the film’s director, Ryan Coogler.
Jonsson, 32, known for roles in Industry, The Long Walk and Alien: Romulus, will play the son of Chadwick Boseman’s T’Challa in the third Black Panther movie.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Industry star David Jonsson to play Black Panther in Marvel sequel

articles.author: Hannah Ellis-Petersen in Delhi
articles.description:
Ally forced to resign, with opposition parties reinvigorated and strongman leader’s grip over media channels rocked
Even the night before Narendra Modi accepted the resignation of his education minister, India’s prime minister appeared confident that the largest mass uprising to take place in his 12 years in power would do little to rattle his government.
Addressing his “young friends” in a late-night Instagram selfie reel on Friday, he thanked the people – who were mobilised en masse across the country, shouting anti-government slogans – for their “thoughtful suggestions”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: India’s Cockroach Janta party protest victory signals trouble ahead for Modi

articles.author: Helena Smith in Athens
articles.description:
Mythical home of the ancient Greek gods designated alongside the D-day landing beaches in Normandy
After a 12-year wait, Mount Olympus, the mythical home of the ancient Greek gods, has been inducted into a hall of more modern fame as Unesco announced it would be added to its world heritage list.
Greece’s highest mountain made the list alongside the second world war D-day landing beaches in northern France and the ancient Japanese capitals of Asuka and Fujiwara. South Sudan’s Boma-Badingilo landscape, host to one of the world’s largest land mammal migrations, also won a designation – a first for the east African country.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Joy in Greece as Mount Olympus joins Unesco list of world heritage sites

articles.author: Deborah Cole in Berlin
articles.description:
Authorities issue wanted notice for Abdul Ballout, 21, after deadly van ramming described as Islamist terrorism
German authorities have issued a wanted notice for a suspect in a deadly van ramming near Berlin’s Pride festival that has been described as an Islamist attack.
The interior minister, Alexander Dobrindt, named the chief suspect as 21-year-old Abdul Ballout. German media reported he was a supporter of Islamic State with a criminal conviction in May.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Police hunt for suspect after one killed and 16 injured in attack at Berlin Pride

articles.author: Josh Butler
articles.description:
Exclusive: Malcolm Roberts uses white supremacist concept to describe the party’s plans for deporting 200,000 people from Australia

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Senator Malcolm Roberts claims One Nation wants to deport at least 200,000 people and has repeatedly referred to the far-right concept of “remigration” in podcast interviews and speeches to niche platforms.
In two recent podcasts, Roberts said One Nation wanted to deport 100,000 temporary residents as well as 100,000 international students – a total much higher than the party’s published policy. The senator said after those people were removed, he wanted to “start working on the higher numbers of people we need to get rid of”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Get rid of them’: One Nation senator claims party will ‘remigrate’ illegal visa holders in resurfaced interview

articles.author: Yohannes Lowe (now) and Wendy Frew (earlier)
articles.description:
Fires displace people on massive scale and trigger one of the largest peacetime civilian evacuation operations ever carried out in France

More than 250,000 people flee wildfires in France and Spain

As my colleagues note in this story, scientists say climate breakdown is triggering more frequent and more extreme weather events, evaporating soils and waterways, fuelling wildfires and leading to thousands of excess deaths. Europe is heating at about twice the global average rate.
Spain’s environment ministry has said that 32 major forest fires have been recorded so far this year, compared with seven over the same period in 2025.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Europe wildfires: ‘Difficult hours lie ahead’ in battle to contain fires, says Pedro Sánchez as more than 300,000 flee homes in France and Spain – as it happened

articles.author: José Olivares in New York
articles.description:
Exclusive: CSI Aviation and GlobalX accused of violating civil rights as part of Trump immigration crackdown
Venezuelan men sent last year to a notorious Salvadorian terrorism prison by the Trump administration are suing the US aviation companies that transported them there.
A lawsuit filed this week in federal court in Washington DC accuses the companies CSI Aviation and GlobalX of violating the Venezuelans’ civil rights, false imprisonment, intentional infliction of emotional distress, negligence and other violations, for their role in flying the three planes that took the men to El Salvador.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Venezuelan men sue aviation firms who flew them to notorious Salvadorian jail

articles.author: Hannah Ellis-Petersen in Delhi
articles.description:
Dharmendra Pradhan steps down after demonstrations over exam leak scandal, prompting celebrations among thousands of protesters
India’s education minister, Dharmendra Pradhan, has resigned after a week of mass demonstrations, handing a major victory to a new youth movement that has posed an unprecedented challenge to Narendra Modi’s government.
In a statement on Saturday afternoon, Pradhan said he had submitted his letter of resignation to the prime minister after student pressure.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: India’s education minister resigns in victory for Cockroach youth movement protests

articles.author: Amrit Dhillon in Delhi
articles.description:
Bollywood stars accused of ‘cowardice’ as hundreds of thousands of young Indians take to the streets to challenge government
Bollywood stars and other Indian celebrities have faced fierce criticism for staying silent in the face of some of the biggest protests India has seen in years.
Hundreds of thousands of young Indians took to the streets this week as part of a new youth movement that calls itself the Cockroach Janata party (CJP), demanding accountability over exam paper leaks in an unprecedented challenge to prime minister Narendra Modi’s government. Many vented their anger against what they saw as “cowardice” from India’s biggest celebrities.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Indian celebrities fiercely criticised for silence on Cockroach protests

articles.author: William Christou
articles.description:
Saudi air defences intercept ballistic missiles as Iran reports first night without US strikes in two weeks
Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthi rebels claimed a missile attack on the southern Saudi city of Jizan on Saturday, after vowing retaliation against the kingdom for attacks this week.
Iran, meanwhile, reported no strikes overnight on Saturday for the first time after two weeks of US attacks. The Iranian health ministry spokesperson, Hossein Kermanpour, said: “Iran had a peaceful night” in a post on X. Tensions, however, remain high.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Iran-backed Houthis claim missile attack on Saudi Arabia as regional tensions escalate

articles.author: Nicola Davis Science correspondent
articles.description:
Jewellery made from BC Iran worn at Odyssey photocall throws spotlight on the trade of rare archeological finds
The Odyssey has stormed cinemas, but while its take on the Homeric epic has created ripples among western classicists, it is an actor’s earrings that have made waves further afield.
Zendaya, who portrays the goddess Athena in the movie, provoked outrage when she appeared at a London photocall wearing earrings that were allegedly made from Iranian artefacts dating back to the 1st millennium BC.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Treasure as trinkets: Zendaya’s earrings renew debate on ownership of ancient artefacts

articles.author: Kaamil Ahmed
articles.description:
‘I can’t tolerate this life,’ said the 24-year-old in his last voice message to his relatives. Attacked by the military, a rebel army and criminal gangs, Siraz Ullah risked all for a better future
The fear was audible as he spoke, recording a message to his family, asking for their prayers. After pressing send, 24-year-old Siraz Ullah boarded a boat he hoped could deliver him from the violence and persecution surrounding him at home in Myanmar.
Instead, Siraz is among 500 Rohingya refugees who have vanished at sea after setting sail for Malaysia in late June.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Family of missing Rohingya footballer fear he is among 500 believed dead in Myanmar shipwrecks

articles.author: Seham Tantesh in Gaza and Emma Graham-Harrison in Jerusalem; photographs by Amjed Tantesh
articles.description:
In sea pools built with sandbags and rubble, Amjed Tantesh gives traumatised children brief respite from their daily lives
Swimming classes have started again in Gaza after three years of war, with hundreds of children learning to float, doggy paddle and take their first strokes in five makeshift sea pools built from sandbags and rubble.
The lessons allow a few hundred girls and boys to reclaim their childhood for a few hours in a place where there are no playgrounds, no formal education and children live in fear of continuing Israeli attacks. A UN survey in March found that 96% of children felt death was imminent.
Activity on the Gaza seafront
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Reclaiming stolen childhoods: swimming classes resume in Gaza after three years of war

articles.author: Reuters in Toronto
articles.description:
At least 90 active blazes in British Columbia in what PM says is one of the country’s most intense seasons on record

How dangerous are wildfires and how can we stop them from getting worse?

Fresh wildfires have broken out in western Canada and forests continued to ⁠burn in Ontario as the country ⁠battled what the prime ​minister, Mark Carney, called one of the most intense wildfire seasons on record.
Nearly 34,000 lightning strikes over the past week led to a series of fires ⁠and evacuation orders in southern British Columbia. There were 25 evacuation orders and 90 active wildfires in the province as of Friday morning, and authorities said warming ⁠and drying conditions could cause them to grow.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Thousands of lightning strikes trigger fresh wildfires in western Canada

articles.author: Associated Press in Georgetown
articles.description:
Of the estimated 179 people aboard, 76 were rescued as efforts continue to salvage the ship and recover all bodies
The confirmed death toll from the recent capsizing of a state ferry off Guyana’s coast has risen to 72, with more bodies recovered as a multinational team struggle to salvage the partially submerged vessel.
Of the estimated 179 people aboard, 76 people were rescued. The government has estimated that 100 may have died in the accident, which would make it the worst marine tragedy on record for the South American nation.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Guyanese authorities confirm death of 72 people in sinking of coastal ferry

articles.author: Hannah Ellis-Petersen in Delhi
articles.description:
Sonam Wangchuk secures ‘hard bargain’ with Delhi but talks between government and movement leaders stall
The Cockroach activist Sonam Wangchuk has ended a 26-day hunger strike, as youth-led protests continued to erupt across India and leaders of the movement said there was no breakthrough in talks with the government.
Wangchuk had been fasting since June in solidarity with the Cockroach Janata party (CJP), a new youth-led movement that has been holding mass protests calling for government accountability and the resignation of the education minister, Dharmendra Pradhan, over exam paper leaks. The leaks affected 2 million students in May and have been linked to more than a dozen suicides.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Indian Cockroach activist ends hunger strike after 26 days as protests spread

articles.author: Olivia Bowden in Toronto
articles.description:
US agency is to pay Canadian media company US$125m for use of investigative database to detect ‘immigration fraud’
A Canadian federal opposition party leader has called on Mark Carney’s government to block the latest data-sharing deal between US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and the Canadian media company Thomson Reuters.
Avi Lewis, the federal leader of the New Democratic party (NDP), demanded on Tuesday that Ottawa address the contract and further restrict Canadian corporations from doing business with ICE, after Canada’s National Observer news website reported on the deal.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Canadian government urged to block Thomson Reuters data deal with US ICE

articles.author: Jonathan Watts
articles.description:
Delegation sent to Brasília after gunmen from organised crime group enter homes in western Amazon
Indigenous leaders on the Brazilian-Peruvian border have said their communities are being “taken hostage” by organised crime groups who are running rampant across the region, destroying rainforest, building roads and trafficking drugs.
Earlier this month, masked men armed with semi-automatic weapons entered homes in Apiwtxa, a village in the Kampa do Rio Amônia Indigenous territory, intimidating people and searching for targets.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Masked men invading and taking Amazon communities ‘hostage’ in organised crime surge, say local leaders

articles.author: Rachel Savage in Johannesburg and agencies
articles.description:
The men were convicted over alleged plan to stage coup and organise deadly demonstrations over fuel prices last year
Two Russian men have been found guilty by an Angolan court of terrorism and spying after being accused of planning a coup and helping to organise deadly demonstrations in the southern African country last year.
Lev Lakshtanov and Igor Ratchin were sentenced to eight and 11 years in jail respectively. They had denied the charges, claiming they were in Angola for cultural and business activities.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Two Russian men jailed in Angola for terrorism and spying

articles.author: Hannah Al-Othman North of England correspondent
articles.description:
September exercise called off after Kenya raises concerns over funding and jurisdiction for criminal offences
The British army has been forced to cancel training for its troops in Kenya after the Kenyan government refused to ratify a bilateral defence agreement.
While the UK government wanted to renew the existing agreement, Kenyan lawmakers had sought changes to give local authorities greater powers to hold British soldiers accountable for any offences committed in the country.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: MoD cancels army training in Kenya over powers to prosecute British soldiers

articles.author: Eva Corlett in Wellington
articles.description:
Dunedin will be the focal point, having last experienced such an eclipse in 1163 – before any humans reached New Zealand
Hotels are booking out two years in advance in the New Zealand city of Dunedin as it prepares for the region’s first total solar eclipse in more than 850 years.
At 4.17pm on 22 July 2028, the moon will pass in front of the sun, casting a roughly 100km-wide shadowy band across parts of southern New Zealand. Everywhere within that band – from tourist hotspot Queenstown in the west to Dunedin city in the east – will be plunged into daytime darkness for 2 minutes and 51 seconds.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Total solar eclipse books out hotels two years in advance in New Zealand city

articles.author: Danny Vincent
articles.description:
Isabel Rose, 26, sentenced to six years for blackmail and perverting course of public justice over her allegations against British man
A British woman who reported being raped to police in Hong Kong has been sentenced to six years in prison for blackmail and perverting the course of public justice.
Isabel Rose, 26, from south-east London, travelled to Hong Kong in early 2024 to visit a British banker she had met while travelling in south-east Asia.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: British woman jailed in Hong Kong for blackmail after accusing banker of rape

articles.author: Sarah Basford Canales and Luca Ittimani
articles.description:
Foreign minister Penny Wong will deliver speech criticising China’s recent launch of a nuclear-capable submarine-launched missile

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Penny Wong will warn China that Australia and other neighbouring nations will not be bullied by its “provocative” actions, after its involvement in another “destabilising and dangerous” incident this week.
The foreign affairs minister – who will deliver the address on Thursday in the Philippines, where the 59th Asean foreign minister’s meeting is being held – will also caution world leaders against placing a toll on the strait of Hormuz after both Iran and the US threatened to do amid the protracted conflict.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Australia to warn China it won’t be bullied by ‘provocative‘ actions as it builds military and nuclear arsenal

articles.author: Raphael Rashid
articles.description:
Prosecutors seek a one-year sentence and heavy fine after chef garnished dish with insects not approved for consumption
Prosecutors in South Korea have asked a court to sentence the owner of a Michelin-starred restaurant to one year in prison for serving a dessert topped with ants, an insect not approved for consumption under local food safety law.
The request, made on Monday, also sought a 20m won (£10,108) fine for the company that runs the restaurant, Yonhap news agency reported.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Michelin-starred restaurant owner in South Korea faces jail over ant dessert

articles.author: Gavin Blair in Tokyo
articles.description:
In April Japan coined new term kokushobi for days above 40C as country advises workers to wear shorts to the office to cope with stifling heat
Japan logged its first official kokushobi or “cruelly hot day” on Tuesday since the new term for when temperatures top 40 degrees Celsius was introduced in April. The Japan Meteorological Agency coined the new designation to warn the public of the heat dangers of days that were once freak weather events but have now become more common.
The central Japan cities of Gujo and Tajimi in Gifu prefecture, along with Toyota in Aichi prefecture, all hit 40C. Gujo’s 40C and Toyota’s 40.1C were all-time highs recorded at their respective weather stations.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Japan records its first ‘cruelly hot day’ as cities swelter in 40-degree heat

articles.author: Nadeem Badshah
articles.description:
UK resident was evacuated from Democratic Republic of the Congo where there is an outbreak of the disease
A humanitarian worker is being monitored at a specialist hospital in London after potential exposure to the Ebola virus.
The UK resident was medically evacuated from the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) where the worker had been treating patients with the disease, the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) said.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Health worker monitored for Ebola in London hospital after working in DRC

articles.author: Kat Lay Global health correspondent
articles.description:
Global hunger declined for the third year in a row in 2025 but experts call for action to bring down costs of fruit, vegetables and dairy as report shows 2.69bn people can’t afford to eat well
One in three people cannot afford to eat a healthy diet, a new report has found, prompting calls for urgent action on food affordability.
There are 2.69 billion people unable to afford a diverse diet that meets their energy and nutrient needs, and it will take “immense” amounts of work to achieve the global target of zero hunger by 2030, the annual report from five UN agencies warned.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Healthy diet too expensive for one in three people globally, UN report finds

articles.author: Eromo Egbejule in Abidjan
articles.description:
Incumbent Carlos Vila Nova hopes to defeat his former party and secure second term as independent
Voters in São Tomé and Príncipe go to the polls for a presidential election on Sunday as one of Africa’s least populous countries seeks to burnish its democratic credentials.
According to the National Election Commission, about 142,000 people are registered to vote in the tiny African state’s elections, approximately 15% of whom live in the diaspora.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: São Tomé and Príncipe heads to polls in tense presidential election

articles.author: Marina Dunbar
articles.description:
Figures are source of dispute as US defense department days ago reduced record of troops killed and wounded
The Pentagon updated its official war casualty database over the weekend, adding more than 140 wounded service members. The Defense Casualty Analysis System (DCAS) also introduced a new casualty category labeled “Overseas Operations” for personnel killed and wounded “starting July 7”.
According to the updated database, the official toll for the earlier phase of the US-Iran war, known as Operation Epic Fury, now stands at 14 service members killed and more than 400 wounded in action.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Pentagon reports more than 600 Iran war casualties in quiet database update

articles.author: Associated Press
articles.description:
Israeli prime minister says ICC’s war crime charges are ‘bogus’ and plans to be in New York for UN gathering this fall
Benjamin Netanyahu said on Sunday that Zohran Mamdani, the New York City mayor, is “fomenting hate” by calling the Israeli prime minister a war criminal who should be arrested over Israel’s war in Gaza if he visits the city for the United Nations general assembly.
Netanyahu said he intends to be in New York in September to address the annual UN gathering of world leaders, despite the mayor’s suggestion that he is not welcome. Mamdani said on Wednesday that while New York City does not have legal authority to execute an arrest warrant issued by the world’s top war crimes court, he encouraged the federal government to do so.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Netanyahu accuses Mamdani of ‘fomenting hate’ in calls for PM’s arrest

articles.author: Marina Dunbar
articles.description:
Scott Gottlieb responds to report that company contacted the White House seeking to delay a recall announcement
Former Food and Drug Administration commissioner Dr Scott Gottlieb said on Sunday that it was “not standard operating procedure” for Taylor Farms to ask the White House to intervene as the company prepared to announce a recall tied to a massive cyclospora outbreak.
Appearing on CBS’s Face the Nation, Gottlieb was asked about a report from the Wall Street Journal that Taylor Farms contacted the White House seeking to delay a recall announcement while federal investigators were preparing to publicly link the company to the multi-state outbreak.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Not standard’ for Taylor Farms to ask White House to delay cyclospora recall, ex-FDA head says

articles.author: Maya Yang
articles.description:
Tom Homan comments on officer’s eligibility to serve after reports that agent’s two ex-wives had accused him of abuse
Tom Homan, the Trump administration “border czar”, on Sunday said he did not believe the Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officer at the center of a recent fatal shooting in Maine “should have ever cleared vetting”.
Speaking to CNN’s State of the Union, Homan was asked by host Dana Bash about the officer’s eligibility to serve following reports that two of his ex-wives had accused him of abuse.
The Associated Press contributed reporting
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump ‘border czar’ says ICE officer in Maine killing should not have cleared vetting

articles.author: Marina Dunbar
articles.description:
Singer rebukes Trump administration after it uses her song Firework over footage of missile striking Iranian naval ship
Pop star Katy Perry has condemned the Trump White House after it used her hit song Firework in a TikTok video showing US military strikes on Iranian targets, saying she never approved the use of her music.
The White House video, which featured Firework playing over footage of a missile striking an Iranian naval ship, has amassed more than 6 million views. The post was captioned: “Iran has been warned.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Katy Perry ‘deeply appalled’ over White House using her song in Iran war video

articles.author: Editorial
articles.description:
Even if no reactors are built, Donald Trump’s announcement of a double-standards deal with Riyadh has wrought further damage in a new era of proliferation
Even as he threatened to escalate an unlawful war sold in part as preventing Iran from gaining a nuclear weapon, Donald Trump opened the door to proliferation in the region on Wednesday. The US announced that it had signed a deal with Saudi Arabia which would potentially allow the kingdom to enrich uranium in future and to avoid the fullest inspection rights for the international watchdog.
Experts have long warned that a civilian nuclear programme could create a path towards a nuclear-armed Riyadh. Mohammed bin Salman, the Saudi crown prince and de facto leader, has said that if Tehran gets a nuclear weapon, “we will have to get one”. Concerns are magnified by the agreement’s terms. Washington previously argued that the “gold standard” was the United Arab Emirates’ agreement to permanently forgo enrichment and accept full monitoring by the UN’s International Atomic Energy Agency. Weakening it sets a precedent that Russia or China could also cite in nuclear deals in future.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: The Guardian view on a US-Saudi nuclear agreement: an offer that further erodes international safeguards | Editorial

articles.author: Michael Sainato
articles.description:
More than 330,000 Haitian immigrants in limbo as Trump administration seeks to end temporary protected status
More than 330,000 Haitian immigrants in the US are set to lose their ability to legally live and work in the country as the Trump administration seeks to terminate their temporary protected status. An estimated 13,000 are nursing assistants, who care for 65,000 patients every day.
“I get up at 5am every morning and I take two buses to work to clean the rooms of the residents. I give my heart,” said a nursing home housekeeper with TPS from Haiti, who requested to remain anonymous for fear of retaliation. “These residents are like my grandmother.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘We’re human beings’: Haitians in the US fear family separation and deportation to violence

articles.author: Robert Tait in Washington
articles.description:
President harks back to red scare of his childhood to attack US left – but will such language resonate beyond Maga base?
Perhaps above all else, Donald Trump is a child of the cold war.
Three months before the US president was born, Winston Churchill delivered a historic speech in Fulton, Missouri, that ushered in a generations-long existential struggle between western capitalism and Soviet communism.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump revives old tropes as he pushes warnings of ‘communist menace’

articles.author: George Chidi
articles.description:
The president really has no power over elections – but that hasn’t stopped Trump from laying the groundwork to challenge results in November
When Donald Trump commandeered primetime US television last Friday, he delivered a familiar, but still extraordinary, message. The president argued once again that the results of the 2020 election, which he lost to Joe Biden, were illegitimate.
US elections are “vulnerable to being rigged and stolen”, Trump alleged, claiming that “the trust of the American people was lost” when he was defeated.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: How Trump could undermine the midterms

articles.author: Arwa Mahdawi
articles.description:
A new report shows more Senate-confirmed staffers have left their jobs this time around than in his first term
Donald Trump loves a construction project. He’s building a ballroom, revamping a reflecting pool, and overseeing the construction of a skyline-altering arch in Washington DC. For his next real estate scheme, may I suggest a giant revolving door in the White House? It would certainly get a lot of use: senior officials are leaving Trump’s second administration at record rates.
According to a new report called Quiet Chaos by the nonpartisan Partnership for Public Service, 27 Senate-confirmed officials have left their positions within cabinet departments to date. That’s nearly 150% higher than the 11 departures in the first 18 months of Trump’s first administration. Per the report, it is also “nearly two and a half times as many as Trump’s first administration (11) and over six times as many as the average between the George W Bush, Barack Obama and Joe Biden administrations (4.3)”.
Arwa Mahdawi is a Guardian columnist
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Staff turnover is rampant under Trump 2.0 – with insidious results | Arwa Mahdawi

articles.author: Douglas Main in Tucson, Arizona
articles.description:
Environmental groups are sounding the alarm over plans that threaten a desert spring that’s home to rare fish and turtles and sacred to the O’odham people
Quitobaquito Springs in south-west Arizona has been called a biological wonderland with few equals.
The springs are an oasis in the vast Sonoran desert along the US-Mexico border, held sacred by the O’odham people, who call it A’al Vaipia. Here, water flows out of an aquifer at the bottom of a hill, runs along a short concrete channel and collects in a pond.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: This desert oasis is a biological wonderland. Trump’s border wall threatens to destroy it

articles.author: Eduardo Porter
articles.description:
Forced labor is a problem, especially in the US, where prisoners are coerced to work for pennies – or nothing at all

US politics live – latest updates

Don’t believe the Trump administration’s rationale for its new volley of tariffs against everybody.
The new levies, ostensibly to punish countries for failing to do enough to curb forced labor, switched on at 12.01am on Friday, to coincide with the expiration of a temporary 10% blanket duty that Donald Trump imposed in February, ostensibly to protect the United States from a balance-of-payments crisis.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: If Trump really cares about forced labor, he should look at the US – rather than slap more tariffs on the world | Eduardo Porter

articles.author: Lateefah Simon and Guillermo Mayer
articles.description:
The US will no longer hold transportation agencies accountable for unintentional discrimination. That’s devastating for those of us who depend on it
As the first congenitally blind member of Congress and a former president of the Bay Area Rapid Transit (Bart) board, I know that the ability to move – to get to work, to school, to the doctor – is a freedom our nation’s civil rights laws have long promised to protect. Last month, the Trump administration derailed that promise.
Through a regulatory maneuver designed to evade public scrutiny, the Department of Transportation announced it will no longer hold transportation agencies accountable when their decisions produce discriminatory outcomes – no matter how severe – so long as the discrimination was unintentional. As a result, decades of civil rights protection were erased by regulatory fiat.
Congresswoman Lateefah Simon represents California’s 12th congressional district in the East Bay. She is the first congenitally blind member to serve in Congress and a strong advocate for transportation and disability justice. She previously served as Bart president and executive director of the San Francisco Lawyers Committee for Civil Rights
Guillermo Mayer is an attorney and the president and CEO of Public Advocates, a 55-year old civil rights law firm and advocacy organization dedicated to challenging the systemic causes of poverty and racial discrimination
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Public transit is a lifeline for countless Americans. Trump is derailing our protections | Lateefah Simon and Guillermo Mayer

articles.author: Hosted by Kai Wright and Carter Sherman , with David Smith and Rachel Leingang . Produced by Suzanne Gaber and Tiara Chiaramonte , edited by Anabel Bacon , engineered by Ivan Kuraev
articles.description:
Earlier this year, Congress reached a depressing milestone: 86% of Americans, a record high, disapproved of its job performance. But this summer, there have been some signs that shifts are underway. On the left, House Democrats have just voted in unprecedented numbers to withhold military aid from Israel, and across the country, progressive candidates are running competitive primary campaigns that are energizing a base fed up with the status quo. On the right, Republicans are reeling from the sudden death of Lindsey Graham, the South Carolina senator and one of Donald Trump's staunchest supporters. Mitch McConnell, the former Senate majority leader, remains sequestered following a health scare in June, raising questions of if a changing of the guard might be underway there, too. Kai Wright and Carter Sherman are joined by David Smith, the Guardian's Washington bureau chief and Rachel Leingang, midwest political correspondent, to discuss gerontocracy, transparency, the rise of the Democratic Socialists of America and just how much of an inflection point this summer might be for both parties


This page was amended on 23 July 2026. A previous version misspelled Lindsey Graham. 

 Continue reading...
articles.title: Is US Congress finally on the verge of a change? – Stateside with Kai and Carter

articles.author: Sam Levine Zhara Keogh Michael Kalenderian Sarah Bertram
articles.description:
Donald Trump delivered a primetime address to the country on Thursday, claiming that declassified intelligence showed Chinese interference in US elections. The US president revived long-running attacks on election security, despite a US intelligence assessment that found no evidence Beijing altered the 2020 vote, which he lost. The Guardian's voting rights reporter Sam Levine factchecks some of Trump's claims

Trump is invoking foreign election interference to justify his own - Opinion

 Continue reading...
articles.title: Fact-checking Donald Trump’s address on Chinese election interference – video

articles.author: Hosted by Jonathan Freedland . Produced by May Robson, Jacob Liebenberg, Ned Carter Miles and the executive producer is Maz Ebtehaj .
articles.description:
The debate about how old is too old to serve in public office has resurfaced this week after the shock death of the Republican senator Lindsey Graham and the surprise return of Mitch McConnell, the 84-year-old senator who published a photo of himself in hospital after a long absence from the spotlight.
With rumours continuing to swirl around Donald Trump’s health, why is it US politicians seem to cling on to power for so long?
Jonathan Freedland speaks to Alexis Coe, a presidential historian and columnist for the New York Times Book review, about whether the US is becoming a gerontocracy – and what can be done about it
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Are American politicians too old? | Politics Weekly America

articles.author: Hosted by Kai Wright and Carter Sherman , with Shrai Popat and Lauren Gambino . Produced by Meg Driscoll, edited by Anabel Bacon , engineered by Ivan Kuraev
articles.description:
Earlier this week, Graham Platner, the Democratic candidate for Senate in Maine, was accused by a former partner of sexual assault. Platner denies the allegations, but on Wednesday, he suspended his campaign, accusing the “political establishment” of tanking his candidacy. But this is only the most recent scandal to have surfaced around Platner’s campaign — over the past year, the oyster farmer and combat veteran was revealed to have a tattoo that closely resembled a Totenkopf (a widely recognized Nazi symbol), a long paper trail of racist, misogynist and homophobic posts on Reddit, and in June, the New York Times published allegations from three former partners about Platner’s “toxic” behavior in their relationships, including, in several cases, physical intimidation (allegations Platner denied).
As Democrats regroup and evaluate their dwindling chances to flip the Senate in November, hosts Kai Wright and Carter Sherman are joined by Guardian political reporters Lauren Gambino and Shrai Popat to ask why voters flocked to Platner, why they were reluctant to abandon him as the scandals came out — and what the whole mess says about who gets the privilege of political redemption.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Why Graham Platner wasn’t the answer to the Democrats’ man problem – Stateside with Kai and Carter

articles.author: Presented by Nosheen Iqbal with Lucas Amin; produced by Natalie Ktena, Belinda Gurung and Ross Burns; executive producer Sami Kent
articles.description:
The investigative journalist Lucas Amin reports on how the tech company Palantir won a £330m contract with the NHS … and what happened once its software was introduced
How did Palantir – sometimes described as ‘the world’s scariest company’ – start working with the NHS?
The investigative journalist Lucas Amin shares the findings of his and his colleague Peter Geoghegan’s investigation into the tech company and its relationship with the UK’s public health service – and tells a story of controversial politicians, paid-for political access, and shocking loopholes in UK lobbying regulations.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: How Palantir got into the NHS - podcast

articles.author: Josh Halliday North of England editor
articles.description:
PM urged to end ‘cover-up culture’ and order independent review taking in evidence that has emerged on 1994 crash
The families of those killed in an RAF Chinook crash in 1994 have urged Andy Burnham to end Britain’s “cover-up culture” and order an independent review into the disaster.
Twenty-nine serving military personnel died when the Chinook HC2 helicopter crashed on the Mull of Kintyre in south-west Scotland during a flight from Northern Ireland.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: RAF Chinook crash victims’ families ask Andy Burnham for review of disaster

articles.author: Phillip Inman
articles.description:
Bank of England expected to keep rates on hold on Thursday but renewed Iran conflict casts shadow over energy costs
The Bank of England could be forced to tear up its economic forecasts and raise interest rates later this year if oil prices return to above $100 a barrel, according to City economists.
Before a meeting of Bank officials on Thursday, economists said that while an interest rate hike would probably be avoided this week there could be some in the future because of conflict in the Middle East.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Rising oil prices could force up UK interest rates, say economists

articles.author: Nadeem Badshah
articles.description:
Four others arrested on suspicion of same murder in Luton after death of 17-year-old
A 16-year-old boy has been charged with murdering a teenager who died from multiple stab wounds at a park in Luton, police said.
Four other teenagers have been arrested on suspicion of the same murder.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Boy, 16, charged with murder of teenager stabbed in Luton park

articles.author: Jamie Grierson
articles.description:
Airport’s bars and restaurants were also unable to serve drinks to passengers because of lack of running water
Water supply has been restored to most of Gatwick airport after passengers spent hours without access to working toilets, and bars and restaurants were closed.
Most toilets had reopened across both terminals on Sunday evening, with the remaining facilities, including bars and restaurants, expected to return to normal for the first of Monday’s flights.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Water supply restored to Gatwick airport after hours without working toilets

articles.author: Peter Walker Senior political correspondent
articles.description:
Ukrainian president will be first overseas visitor for new British prime minister
Volodymyr Zelenskyy will become Andy Burnham’s first overseas visitor as prime minister, in a visit that Burnham said underlined Britain’s “unwavering” backing for Ukraine.
Less than two weeks after Keir Starmer travelled to Kyiv for the final foreign visit of his prime ministership, the Ukrainian president will on Monday join Burnham at a naval base where Ukrainian forces have been receiving training.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Burnham to meet Zelenskyy at UK naval base in show of ‘unwavering’ support

articles.author: Nadeem Badshah and agencies
articles.description:
Director Ryan Coogler announces British actor in lead role alongside co-stars Letitia Wright and Winston Duke

The British actor David Jonsson has been unveiled as the new Black Panther by the film’s director, Ryan Coogler.
Jonsson, 32, known for roles in Industry, The Long Walk and Alien: Romulus, will play the son of Chadwick Boseman’s T’Challa in the third Black Panther movie.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Industry star David Jonsson to play Black Panther in Marvel sequel

articles.author: Ian Sample Science editor
articles.description:
King’s Fund report finds men and women live, on average, for 80 years and nearly 84 years, but gains are in south
The north-south divide in life expectancy in England has grown over the past decade, with people in northern regions facing more illnesses such as heart disease and cancer, but also suicides and deaths related to alcohol and drug misuse.
Provisional figures show life expectancy reached an all-time high in 2025, with men and women in England living, on average, for 80 years and nearly 84 years respectively, but the gains were overwhelmingly in the south, the King’s Fund said.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: England’s north-south life expectancy gap grows despite record longevity

articles.author: Gwyn Topham
articles.description:
Former City trader’s weekly Gary’s Economics videos took off during the Covid pandemic
The City trader turned wealth tax campaigner Gary Stevenson has announced he is quitting the YouTube channel that made his name, citing health concerns.
His announcement, in a 48-minute address to camera, came after a mixed reaction to a televised documentary that brought him to a wider audience but drew some scepticism from left-leaning tax experts as well as more rightwing critics.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Gary Stevenson to quit YouTube channel, citing health concerns

articles.author: Pippa Crerar and Alexandra Topping
articles.description:
From TikTok appearances to ‘sugar rush’ policies, new prime minister is taking different approach to predecessor
Six weeks ago Andy Burnham was not even an MP; now the former mayor of Greater Manchester is the most important political figure in Britain. After orchestrating a bloodless coup against Keir Starmer, in which he was crowned as Labour leader unopposed, the new prime minister has started his tenure in Downing Street with some eye-catching policies and a radically different approach to communication. A week into the job, how do their leadership styles compare?
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Burnham v Starmer: one week in, how do their leadership styles compare?

articles.author: Diane Taylor
articles.description:
Union calls for museum to become accredited London living wage employer and let staff carry water during shifts
Workers at one of the world’s leading art and design museums are balloting for “heatwave” strike action.
The ballot at V&A is taking place because of concerns about soaring temperatures and access to drinking water, along with pay and conditions.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: V&A workers hold ballot to strike over pay and heatwave conditions

articles.author: Ian Sample Science editor
articles.description:
Preliminary study shows older people who avoided food four hours before bed did better in problem solving tests
Confining mealtimes and snacks to a nine-hour window and avoiding food for four hours before bed may help stave off cognitive decline in older age, researchers say.
A pilot study of older women living with overweight or obesity found hints of improvement in mental skills among those who ate within the restricted period compared with those who spread their meals over a longer time.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Restricted eating hours may reduce cognitive decline in older age, researchers find

articles.author: Esther Addley
articles.description:
PM’s team can be seen as backward step even though in some ways it is more diverse. Yet its makeup points to wider access to power

Race, school, gender: the makeup of Andy Burnham’s cabinet – in charts

Like 20 British prime ministers before him, Andy Burnham’s new cabinet minister for AI, Kanishka Narayan, went to Eton. After graduating from the country’s most elite private school, Narayan attended Balliol College, Oxford, where he studied – what else? – PPE (politics, philosophy and economics), like David Cameron, Rishi Sunak, Ed Miliband and a host of other senior politicians. An MBA at Stanford and a career in the City followed.
But Narayan’s background is hardly typical of the British ruling class. Born in Bihar in eastern India, he moved with his family to Cardiff when he was 12. He and his younger brother were sleeping on the floor of their one-bedroom home when a teacher at his local high school suggested the bright young boy apply for some private schools. His parents, who had joined the Labour party almost as soon as they arrived in Wales, ran a petrol station. Eton was possible only thanks to a full scholarship.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Is Burnham’s Oxbridge-heavy cabinet a sign of social mobility or lack of progress on class?

articles.author: Peter Walker Senior political correspondent
articles.description:
PM promises to ‘defend national interest before anything else’ in first big broadcast interview since entering No 10
Andy Burnham has promised to disagree with Donald Trump if necessary, including in public, in his first big broadcast interview since becoming prime minister.
Burnham’s comments came as Wes Streeting, the new defence secretary, said he did not believe the Trump administration was looking for allies who “suck up”, but rather those with the confidence to set out disagreements when needed.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Andy Burnham says he will disagree with Trump in public if necessary

articles.author: Rob Davies
articles.description:
England’s progress provides best football-related uplift of recent years, with one pub too packed to host its Dolly Parton tribute
Late opening hours and England’s progress to the semi-final of an expanded World Cup helped provide the best football-related uplift of recent years for pubs, figures suggest.
Pubs poured 30m extra pints over the course of the tournament compared with a normal trading period, with busy pumps delivering £150m in added sales, according to the British Beer & Pubs Association (BBPA).
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Weekday games were amazing’: pubs toast extra £150m in World Cup sales

articles.author: Josh Halliday and Priya Bharadia
articles.description:
Polling puts close Burnham ally in lead as she aims to defeat Reform and draw back support from revitalised Greens
Bev Craig was mid-squat at the gym when she was recognised for the first time as the prospective heir to Andy Burnham’s throne. Until recently, the Manchester city council leader could happily have gone about her workout in peace.
But all that changed when Burnham, who DJ’ed at her 40th birthday party last year, won the Makerfield byelection and set up another big electoral contest on his way to becoming prime minister.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘This is the dream job’: Labour’s Bev Craig on the battle to be Manchester mayor

articles.author: Simon Goodley
articles.description:
Adrian Howe’s family believe that fears his deal would be financially ruinous led him to kill himself
The family of a former mobile phone store manager who was found drowned days before his new Vodafone franchise was to open its doors is pressing the government to introduce a new franchising law in his name.
The call comes a week after Vodafone settled a long-running legal claim filed by 62 of its former franchisees who alleged that the company “unjustly enriched” itself at their expense by up to £85m.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Family of former Vodafone manager found drowned call for ‘Adrian’s law’ to protect franchisees

articles.author: Geraldine McKelvie
articles.description:
Scotland Yard is looking at two £250,000 donations to the party by Britain Means Business before the 2024 election
Payments to Reform UK first revealed by the Guardian are now being investigated by the Metropolitan police.
The inquiry is scrutinising payments made to the party via a company controlled by its deputy leader, Richard Tice.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Police investigate payments to Reform UK first revealed by The Guardian

articles.author: Geraldine McKelvie Senior correspondent
articles.description:
Exclusive: Blunder at Rosebank, UK’s biggest undeveloped oilfield, comes as government considers granting licence
Production at Britain’s biggest undeveloped oil and gasfield could be delayed for months after equipment from a rig was accidentally dropped in the North Sea, the Guardian can reveal.
Andy Burnham’s new government is under pressure from the fossil fuel industry to allow oil to be retrieved from the Rosebank site despite opposition from climate campaigners and some Labour MPs.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: New North Sea oil drilling faces delay after gear accidentally dropped in sea

articles.author: Phillip Inman
articles.description:
Sanae Takaichi’s blueprint to inject £1.7tn and double economic growth leaves many investors fearful
International investors are asking where Japan’s prime minister will find the ¥370tn (£1.7tn) of extra cash that she wants to invest in 17 industrial sectors by 2040.
Such is the scale of spending by Sanae Takaichi’s coalition government that many in her own party fear she is about to blow up the Japanese economy, triggering a Liz Truss-style economic shock.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Can Japan avoid a Liz Truss-style shock as its PM embarks on a giant spending spree?

articles.author: Sandra Laville Environment correspondent
articles.description:
Campaigners urge government to introduce right of access to water, particularly as heatwaves become more common
Almost three-quarters of riverbanks in England have no public access, according to data released by the Right to Roam campaign.
Across the country, the public cannot use riverbanks or gain access to the rivers themselves in most of the river catchments from the west of Cornwall up to the Tweed, which flows through northern England and Scotland.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Almost 75% of England’s riverbanks ‘off limits’ to public, figures show

articles.author: Nicola Davis Science correspondent
articles.description:
Research into GLP-1 medications is not always robust but complaints such as digestive problems are well known
Weight loss jabs such as Wegovy and Mounjaro have boomed in popularity, and so have reports of myriad side-effects. This week researchers have suggested GLP-1 medications could be associated with hair loss.
It can be hard to keep tabs on which of these unintentional outcomes have been the subject of expert scrutiny and which remain little more than hearsay. We take a look at some of the most talked about side-effects and explore which have been studied – and which remain unproven.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Ozempic face’ and hair loss: what evidence is there for weight-loss drug side-effects?

articles.author: Rupert Jones
articles.description:
Don’t delay in taking advantage of the competition that is pushing up interest rates and increasing choice, experts say
It is shaping up to be a decent summer for savers as fierce competition among providers pushes up interest rates and increases choice.
You can currently get instant- and easy-access accounts that pay up to 5% interest, and fixed-rate savings bonds that pay almost that much. Meanwhile, those looking for a regular savings account can now get up to 8%.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: UK savings deals: the heat is on as banks offer up to 8%

articles.author: Kiran Stacey and Patrick Butler
articles.description:
Exclusive: Andy Burnham thought to be considering waiving stricter right to remain rules for people already working in the sector
Hundreds of thousands of care workers could be exempted from the home secretary’s plans to toughen up the immigration system under proposals being considered by Andy Burnham as he looks for ways to relieve pressure on the social care sector.
The prime minister will give a speech next week spelling out his determination to start creating a National Care Service before the next general election as he looks to accelerate the process set up by his predecessor, Keir Starmer.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Existing care workers could be exempt from UK’s tough new immigration rules

articles.author: Amelia Hill
articles.description:
Business owners in England say prioritising venues selling alcohol leaves vital community spaces behind 
Ferdinand Geus is proud of the positive, global impact his small speciality coffee business is having.
“Around 3,000 small, family-owned farms in Yemen rely on us – we’ve persuaded many to stop growing khat, the drug, and start growing coffee instead,” said the business manager of Sheba Coffee, which supplies Yemeni coffee beans to independent cafes across the world, including the UK.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘It’s not fair’: cafe owners frustrated over exclusion from business rates cut

articles.author: Jasper Jolly
articles.description:
Exclusive: Eight companies expect to be covered by the ban for 2025-26, the Guardian can reveal
Water company bosses’ total pay rose over the past year despite a government bonus ban and public outrage over pollution and bills, the Guardian can reveal.
One chief executive, Mark Thurston of Anglian Water, received £1.9m – including a £500,000 “retention payment”, despite the bonus ban.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Water bosses’ pay rises despite bonus ban and public fury over bills and pollution

articles.author: Hayden Vernon and agency
articles.description:
Warning in place until Sunday morning in southern and central regions after drought declared in parts of Wales
Heat alerts are in place across parts of England, with possible highs of 30C (86F) and officials saying temperatures are likely to have an impact on health and wellbeing.
The yellow heat health alerts issued for the East Midlands, east of England, London, south-east, south-west and West Midlands are in place until 9am on Sunday.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Parts of England under heat alert with 30C temperatures possible

articles.author: Chloe Mac Donnell
articles.description:
A physio, a tailor and a historian on the style trends that can put women in hospital and how to avoid the dangers
“Buyer beware” is one of the oldest principles in English law. Now, a pair of wide legged trousers from Zara is bringing the phrase back to the forefront of shoppers’ minds.
On social media the £25.99 wide-legged trousers from the high-street retailer have earned the moniker “Zara death pants” thanks to a slew of videos showing wearers tripping over the leg of the trousers and injuring themselves.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: From high heels to ‘Zara death pants’: how fashion falls foul of women’s safety

articles.description:

UK politics live – latest updates

articles.title: Andy Burnham opens No 10 North in Manchester – video

articles.author: Lucy Swan, Kiran Stacey, Carmen Aguilar García and Heidi Wilson
articles.description:
Women have half the seats at the top table for the first time, but Oxbridge maintains its grip
Andy Burnham has appointed the first cabinet of his premiership. Much has been made of how key allies of his predecessor, Keir Starmer, have been demoted or sacked, but what is the demographic makeup of the new team of senior ministers, and how does it differ from other governments?
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Race, school, gender: the makeup of Andy Burnham’s cabinet – in charts

articles.author: Gary Fuller
articles.description:
Team in Ohio finds swapping to electric has ‘very large’ impact, despite study being scaled back by Trump cuts
A US study has found a 70% drop in hospital admissions and days off from work or school when people with poorly controlled asthma had their gas stove and hob replaced with electric.
Ohio’s publicly owned MetroHealth began the study in December 2024 but funding was terminated early by the incoming Trump administration. It had been designed to investigate if replacing gas cooking improved asthma for 1,200 people living near Cleveland, Ohio.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Replacing gas stove can help asthmatics as much as some drugs, US experts find

articles.author: Steven Morris
articles.description:
Black-crowned night heron one of many species thriving at Holnicote Estate where river ‘reset’ has transformed area into lush oasis
A rare black-crowned night heron has been spotted on an estate in the south-west of England where an innovative river “reset” is transforming the area into an oasis for birdlife.
The heron was caught on camera in a jungly corner of the Holnicote Estate, where conservation experts have been restoring the landscape by allowing a river to return to its natural course.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Rare heron seen at Somerset estate where river has been allowed to run free

articles.author: Peter Walker Senior political correspondent
articles.description:
Conservative leader is becoming more confident and forging a message for her party, but faces a new opponent 
“So, Andy Burnham seems like a nice guy.” Those were the slightly unexpected opening words of Kemi Badenoch’s first speech since the change in prime minister. But make no mistake: she was there to bury her opponent.
Even Badenoch-sceptics inside the Conservative party and farther afield agree the Tory leader is becoming more confident, and has been able to forge an increasingly coherent message for her party, one based on a promise of economic competence.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Kemi Badenoch ‘has to adapt’ her rhetoric to take on Andy Burnham

articles.author: Rory Carroll Ireland correspondent
articles.description:
Tribunal rules surveillance aimed at identifying Vincent Kearney’s sources was disproportionate and unlawful
A former BBC journalist has been awarded £20,000 in damages after MI5 and the Police Service of Northern Ireland unlawfully obtained data from his mobile phone.
A specialist tribunal on Thursday ordered the agencies to pay the compensation to Vincent Kearney for attempts to identify his sources while he was the BBC’s Northern Ireland home affairs correspondent.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Ex-BBC journalist awarded £20,000 after MI5 and PSNI unlawfully accessed phone data

articles.author: Bethan McKernan and Sandra Laville
articles.description:
Government agency announces status in north Wales and Upper Severn after series of heatwaves and lack of rainfall
Parts of Wales are now in drought and all other areas of the country are experiencing prolonged dry conditions, with this month on course to be the driest on record for nearly 200 years.
Natural Resources Wales (NRW) said on Thursday that record-low river flows, back-to-back heatwaves and widespread wildfires have prompted the declaration of drought status in north Wales and the Upper Severn.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Drought declared in parts of Wales as July on course to be driest in nearly 200 years

Andy Burnham’s first week in office has seen him announce a range of measures to help people with the cost of living crisis, and scrap several of Keir Starmer’s big policies. 
But critics – including former Starmer ministers – are questioning how they will be funded and whether they go far enough. Pippa and Kiran look at what’s behind Burnham’s policy blitz.

Read Kiran’s article on Andy Burnham’s communication style here

articles.title: All change please: Burnham rips up the Starmer playbook – podcast

articles.author: Hayden Vernon
articles.description:
European Commission says Paramount Skydance’s decision to end Universal venture addresses merger concerns
Paramount Skydance’s £80bn takeover of Warner Brothers took a step closer to being realised after it won conditional approval from the European Union.
The European Commission said Paramount’s offer to ⁠end a film ⁠distribution ​joint venture with Universal Pictures addressed its concerns over the potential merger. As part of its commitments in the EU, Paramount has 13 months from the date of closing the deal to pull out from the venture.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Paramount’s £80bn takeover of Warner Brothers a step closer after EU approval

A rare glimpse of a young puffin emerging from its nest has given conservationists fresh hope for the future of Dorset’s dwindling puffin population. The ‘puffling’ was spotted by volunteers working with the National Trust, who renewed their monitoring efforts at the site in March 2026 to understand why mainland England’s last breeding colony on the south coast was failing to produce chicks. It is the first time in 30 years a puffling sighting has been confirmed at the colony. 

‘A great thrill’: baby puffin is first one seen on Dorset coast in three decades

 Continue reading...
articles.title: First ‘puffling’ sighting in three decades give hope for Dorset's struggling puffin colony – video
